#Rental Share and Owner share of each Metropolis
```{r}
iris_with_population <- st_read("C:/Users/ohdaw/OneDrive/Documents/R_Projects/rental_desert/France/Updated_IRIS_with_Population.shp")

france_rental <- st_read("/Users/ohdaw/OneDrive/Documents/R_Projects/rental_desert/France/france_rental.csv")

# Perform the spatial join using 'st_join'
# This will match geometries based on spatial relationships
iris_with_population_and_rental <- iris_with_population %>%
    left_join(france_rental, by = c("CODE_IR" = "IRIS"))


iris_with_population_and_rental <- iris_with_population_and_rental %>%
  select(-ends_with(".y")) %>%
  # Optionally, rename columns to remove the .x suffix if needed
  rename_with(~ gsub("\\.x$", "", .))

# Convert 'P21_PMEN' to numeric, and handle any coercion warnings
iris_with_population_and_rental$P21_PMEN <- as.numeric(iris_with_population_and_rental$P21_PMEN)

## Convert 'rental_sh' to numeric with proper handling
iris_with_population_and_rental <- iris_with_population_and_rental %>%
  mutate(rental_sh = as.numeric(rental_sh))

# Rejoining and summarizing as intended
top_100_urban_units <- iris_with_population_and_rental %>%
  group_by(UU2020) %>%
  summarize(total_population = sum(P21_PMEN, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_population)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 100)

# Ensure both datasets are data frames
iris_df <- st_drop_geometry(iris_with_population_and_rental)
urban_units_df <- st_drop_geometry(top_100_urban_units)

# Perform a standard join on the 'UU2020' column
france_metro_shares <- iris_df %>%
  left_join(urban_units_df, by = "UU2020") %>%
  group_by(libgeo) %>%
  summarise(
    metro_rental_share = mean(rental_sh, na.rm = TRUE),
    metro_owner_share = 100 - metro_rental_share
  )

# View the resulting summarization
print(france_metro_shares)
```

#Calculating Divergence Value
```{r echo = T, results = 'hide'}
# Ensure column names for joining are correctly cased and named
# Ensure 'rental_sh' and other relevant fields are numeric
iris_with_population_and_rental <- iris_with_population_and_rental %>%
  mutate(rental_sh = as.numeric(rental_sh))

# Ensure both data sets are data frames and adjust any potential mismatches in key names
# If top_100_urban_units or france_metro_shares are sf objects, convert them to data frames first
df_top_100_urban_units <- st_drop_geometry(top_100_urban_units)
df_france_metro_shares <- st_drop_geometry(france_metro_shares)

# Join the data sets based on proper column names, ensuring all are data frames
divergence_values <- iris_with_population_and_rental %>%
  left_join(df_top_100_urban_units, by = "UU2020") %>%
  left_join(df_france_metro_shares, by = "libgeo") %>%  # Assuming consistent key naming
  mutate(
    owner_sh = 100 - rental_sh,  # Calculate owner share
    divergence_value = (
      rental_sh * log(rental_sh / metro_rental_share) +
      owner_sh * log(owner_sh / metro_owner_share)
    )
  ) %>%
  select(libgeo, codgeo, IRIS, UU2020,CODE_IR,rental_sh, owner_sh, divergence_value)  # Correct case of column name "UU2020"
```

#Mapping IRIS-Level Divergence Index Values for Housing Tenure
```{r}
# Load and prepare the shapefile with polygons
iris_with_boundaries <- st_read("C:/Users/ohdaw/OneDrive/Documents/R_Projects/rental_desert/France/Updated_Combined_Data.shp")

# Convert CRS to WGS 84 (EPSG: 4326)
iris_with_boundaries <- st_transform(iris_with_boundaries, crs = 4326)
divergence_values <- st_transform(divergence_values, crs = 4326)

# Assuming divergence_values is a data frame, make it an `sf` object if not already
divergence_values_sf <- st_as_sf(divergence_values, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326, agr = "constant") 

# Ensure divergence_values includes the necessary geometry (join on libgeo if matching)
divergence_values_sf <- divergence_values_sf %>%
  select(CODE_IR, divergence_value)

# Spatial join (ensure correct order and usage)
map_data <- iris_with_boundaries %>%
  st_join(divergence_values_sf, left = TRUE)

# Filter out areas with NA divergence values
map_data <- map_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(divergence_value))

# Calculate unique breaks using quantiles
breaks <- unique(quantile(map_data$divergence_value, probs = seq(0, 1, 0.25), na.rm = TRUE))
if (length(breaks) < 5) {
  breaks <- seq(min(map_data$divergence_value, na.rm = TRUE),
                max(map_data$divergence_value, na.rm = TRUE),
                length.out = 5)
}

# Categorize divergence values
map_data <- map_data %>%
  mutate(
    divergence_category = cut(divergence_value, breaks = breaks,
                              labels = c("Least Divergent", "Second Quartile", "Third Quartile", "Most Divergent"),
                              include.lowest = TRUE, right = FALSE)
  )

# Plot using ggplot2
ggplot(data = map_data) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = divergence_category)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Least Divergent" = "#c6dbef", 
                               "Second Quartile" = "#9ecae1", 
                               "Third Quartile" = "#6baed6", 
                               "Most Divergent" = "#3182bd"),
                    na.value = "grey50", 
                    name = "Divergence Index\nValue (Quartile)") +
  labs(title = "IRIS-Level Divergence Index Values for Housing Tenure") +
  theme_minimal()
```

#Mapping Metropolis-Level Divergence Index Values for Housing Tenure#
```{r}
# Assumes that divergence_values is updated and contains 'UU2020' column

# Load and prepare the metro-level shapefile
metro_shapefile <- st_read("C:/Users/ohdaw/OneDrive/Documents/R_Projects/rental_desert/France/France_maps/uu2020_2024/uu2020_2024.shp")

# Summarizing divergence_values at the metro level by averaging divergence values
metro_divergence <- divergence_values %>%
  group_by(UU2020) %>%
  summarize(avg_divergence_value = mean(divergence_value, na.rm = TRUE))

# Convert metro_divergence to a regular data frame if needed
metro_divergence <- as.data.frame(metro_divergence)

# Join the metro divergence data with the metro shapefile
map_data_metro <- metro_shapefile %>%
  dplyr::left_join(metro_divergence, by = c("uu2020" = "UU2020"))

# Check and filter out areas with NA divergence values if necessary
map_data_metro <- map_data_metro %>%
  filter(!is.na(avg_divergence_value))

# Proceed with calculating breaks and plotting
breaks_metro <- unique(quantile(map_data_metro$avg_divergence_value, probs = seq(0, 1, 0.25), na.rm = TRUE))

if (length(breaks_metro) < 5) {
  breaks_metro <- seq(min(map_data_metro$avg_divergence_value, na.rm = TRUE),
                      max(map_data_metro$avg_divergence_value, na.rm = TRUE),
                      length.out = 5)
}

map_data_metro <- map_data_metro %>%
  mutate(
    divergence_category = cut(
      avg_divergence_value,
      breaks = breaks_metro,
      labels = c("Least Divergent", "Second Quartile", "Third Quartile", "Most Divergent"),
      include.lowest = TRUE,
      right = FALSE
    )
  )

# Plot
ggplot(data = map_data_metro) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = divergence_category)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Least Divergent" = "#c6dbef", 
                               "Second Quartile" = "#9ecae1", 
                               "Third Quartile" = "#6baed6", 
                               "Most Divergent" = "#3182bd"),
                    na.value = "grey50", 
                    name = "Divergence Index\nValue (Quartile)") +
  labs(title = "Metro-Level Divergence Index Values for Housing Tenure") +
  theme_minimal()
```

#Top 10 Divergent Metropolis and Paris
```{r}
metro_divergence <- divergence_values %>%
  group_by(UU2020) %>%
  summarize(
    avg_divergence_value = mean(divergence_value, na.rm = TRUE),
    libgeo = first(libgeo),  # Get the first occurrence of 'libgeo' within each group
    CODE_IRIS = first(CODE_IR)  # Get the first occurrence of 'CODE_IRIS' within each group
  )

# Sort and select top 10 metros based on avg_divergence_value
top_10_metros <- metro_divergence %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_divergence_value)) %>%
  slice(1:10)

# Assume you know the specific UU2020 code for Paris, replace "PARIS_CODE" with the actual code
paris_code <- "00851"  # Replace with actual Paris code

# Check if Paris is included
is_paris_included <- paris_code %in% top_10_metros$UU2020

# If Paris is not included, add it manually
if (!is_paris_included) {
  paris_divergence <- metro_divergence %>%
    filter(UU2020 == paris_code)
  top_10_metros <- bind_rows(top_10_metros, paris_divergence)
}

# Ensure the list is top 10 plus Paris, totaling 11 entries without duplicates
top_10_plus_paris <- top_10_metros %>%
  distinct(UU2020, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Print the list with their divergence values
print("Top 10 Metros and Paris with Divergence Index Value:")
print(top_10_plus_paris)
```

#Top 10 Divergence Index Metropolis in IRIS level
```{r}

# Convert `top_10_plus_paris` to a data frame
top_10_plus_paris_df <- as.data.frame(top_10_plus_paris)

# Convert `divergence_values` to a data frame if it's an sf object
divergence_values_df <- as.data.frame(divergence_values)

# Loop over each metro in top_10_plus_paris
for (metro in top_10_plus_paris_df$UU2020) {
  # Filter IRIS data for each metro
  iris_data <- iris_with_boundaries %>%
    filter(u2020_x == metro)
  
  # Get the corresponding libge_x for the current metro
  metro_name <- unique(iris_data$libge_x)[1]

  # Add divergence categories or other relevant attributes if needed
  iris_data <- iris_data %>%
    left_join(divergence_values_df, by = "CODE_IR") %>%
    mutate(
      divergence_category = case_when(
        divergence_value >= quantile(divergence_value, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "Most Divergent",
        divergence_value >= quantile(divergence_value, 0.5, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "Third Quartile",
        divergence_value >= quantile(divergence_value, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "Second Quartile",
        TRUE ~ "Least Divergent"
      )
    )

  # Create the map plot
  map_plot <- ggplot(data = iris_data) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = divergence_category), color = "black", size = 0.2) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Least Divergent" = "#c6dbef", 
                                 "Second Quartile" = "#9ecae1", 
                                 "Third Quartile" = "#6baed6", 
                                 "Most Divergent" = "#3182bd"),
                      na.value = "grey70", 
                      name = "Divergence Category") +
    labs(
      title = paste("Divergence Index Map for Metro:", metro_name),
      fill = "Divergence Category"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

  # Print the map plot
  print(map_plot)
}
```

```{r}
library(openxlsx) 
# Initialize a list to store data for Excel export
excel_data_list <- list()

# Loop over each metro in top_10_urban_units_dataset
for (metro in top_10_urban_units_dataset$uu2020) {
  
  # Filter IRIS data for the current metro
  iris_data <- iris_with_boundaries %>%
    filter(u2020_x == metro)
  
  # Get the metro name (handle potential NA values)
  metro_name <- unique(iris_data$libge_x)[1]
  
  # Ensure `divergence_values_df` has relevant data before merging
  if (!"CODE_IR" %in% names(divergence_values_df)) {
    stop("Error: `divergence_values_df` must contain `CODE_IR` column.")
  }
  
  # Merge and handle missing values
  iris_data <- iris_data %>%
    left_join(divergence_values_df, by = "CODE_IR") %>%
    mutate(divergence_value = ifelse(is.na(divergence_value), 0, divergence_value)) %>%
    mutate(
      divergence_category = case_when(
        divergence_value >= quantile(divergence_value, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "Most Divergent",
        divergence_value >= quantile(divergence_value, 0.5, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "Third Quartile",
        divergence_value >= quantile(divergence_value, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "Second Quartile",
        TRUE ~ "Least Divergent"
      )
    )

  # Store the processed data for Excel export
  excel_data_list[[paste0(metro_name, "_", metro)]] <- iris_data

excel_data_list <- lapply(excel_data_list, function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.factor), as.character)) %>%  # Convert factors to characters
    mutate(across(where(is.list), ~sapply(., toString))) %>%  # Convert lists to strings
    st_drop_geometry()  # Drop spatial geometry if it's an sf object
})

# Export list of data frames to an Excel file
write.xlsx(excel_data_list, file = "Divergence_Index_Metros_top10populated.xlsx")
```

```{r}
# Function to shorten sheet names dynamically
shorten_sheet_name <- function(metro_name, metro_code) {
  clean_name <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "_", metro_name)  # Clean name by removing special chars
  short_name <- substr(paste0(clean_name, "_", metro_code), 1, 31)  # Ensure it's 31 characters max
  return(short_name)
}

# Initialize a list to store data for Excel export
excel_data_list <- list()

# Loop over each metro in top_100_urban_units_dataset
for (metro in top_100_urban_units_dataset$uu2020) {
  
  # Filter IRIS data for the current metro
  iris_data <- iris_with_boundaries %>%
    filter(u2020_x == metro)
  
  # Get the metro name (handle potential NA values)
  metro_name <- unique(iris_data$libge_x)[1]
  
  # Generate a safe sheet name using the shorten function
  sheet_name <- shorten_sheet_name(metro_name, metro)
  
  # Ensure `divergence_values_df` has relevant data before merging
  if (!"CODE_IR" %in% names(divergence_values_df)) {
    stop("Error: `divergence_values_df` must contain `CODE_IR` column.")
  }
  
  # Merge and handle missing values
  iris_data <- iris_data %>%
    left_join(divergence_values_df, by = "CODE_IR") %>%
    mutate(
      divergence_value = ifelse(is.na(divergence_value), 0, divergence_value),
      divergence_category = case_when(
        divergence_value >= quantile(divergence_value, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "Most Divergent",
        divergence_value >= quantile(divergence_value, 0.5, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "Third Quartile",
        divergence_value >= quantile(divergence_value, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "Second Quartile",
        TRUE ~ "Least Divergent"
      )
    )
  
  # Check if there are any 'list' columns and convert them to strings
  iris_data <- iris_data %>%
    mutate(across(where(function(x) is.list(x)), ~sapply(., toString)))  # Convert lists to strings
  
  # Handle potential NaN values by replacing them with 0
  iris_data <- iris_data %>%
    mutate(across(where(function(x) any(is.nan(x))), ~ifelse(is.nan(.), 0, .)))  # Replace NaN with 0
  
  # Store the processed data for Excel export using the cleaned sheet name
  excel_data_list[[sheet_name]] <- iris_data
  
  # Save the plot as an image
  ggsave(filename = paste0("top_100pop_divergence_map_", metro, ".png"), plot = map_plot, width = 10, height = 6)
}

# Export list of data frames to an Excel file
write.xlsx(excel_data_list, file = "Divergence_Index_Metros_top100populated.xlsx")
``` 

```{r echo = T, results = 'hide'}
# Step 1: Filter and Prepare Data
# Filter the divergence values for the top metros including Paris
selected_uu2020 <- top_10_plus_paris$UU2020

# Include all necessary columns and calculate quartiles
iris_divergence_selected_df <- divergence_values %>%
  filter(UU2020 %in% selected_uu2020) %>%
  select(CODE_IR,libgeo, rental_sh, owner_sh, UU2020, divergence_value) %>%
  group_by(UU2020) %>%
  mutate(
    divergence_quartile = ntile(divergence_value, 4)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Step 2: Load IRIS boundaries
iris_boundaries <- st_read("C:/Users/ohdaw/OneDrive/Documents/R_Projects/rental_desert/France/Updated_Combined_Data.shp")

# Ensure columns match for joining
map_data_iris <- iris_boundaries %>%
  left_join(iris_divergence_selected_df, by = "CODE_IR") %>%
  filter(UU2020 %in% selected_uu2020)

# Step 3: Categorization based on quartiles
map_data_iris <- map_data_iris %>%
  mutate(
    divergence_category = case_when(
      divergence_quartile == 4 & rental_sh > owner_sh ~ "Most Divergent, High-Rental",
      divergence_quartile == 4 & rental_sh <= owner_sh ~ "Most Divergent, High-Owner",
      divergence_quartile < 4 & rental_sh > owner_sh ~ "Less Divergent, High-Rental",
      TRUE ~ "Less Divergent, High-Owner"
    )
  )
```

```{r}
# Identify top 10 metros by population
```

#Divergence of Housing Tenure Is Associated with Income Segregation
```{r}
# Load income data
income_data <- read_csv("/Users/ohdaw/OneDrive/Documents/R_Projects/rental_desert/France/Updated_IRIS_with_Income.csv")

# Categorize IRISs into income brackets based on median income
income_data <- income_data %>%
  mutate(
    income_category = case_when(
      DEC_MED21 < 20000 ~ "Lower",
      DEC_MED21 >= 20000 & DEC_MED21 < 40000 ~ "Middle",
      DEC_MED21 >= 40000 ~ "Higher"
    )
  )

# Calculate the share of each category per metro
income_shares <- income_data %>%
  group_by(UU2020, income_category) %>%
  summarize(count = n()) %>%
  group_by(UU2020) %>%
  mutate(
    share = count / sum(count)
  ) %>%
  select(UU2020, income_category, share)

# Calculate metro-level shares for income categories
metro_shares <- income_shares %>%
  group_by(income_category) %>%
  summarize(metro_share = mean(share, na.rm = TRUE))

# Calculate income divergence index
income_divergence <- income_shares %>%
  left_join(metro_shares, by = "income_category") %>%
  mutate(
    divergence_component = share * log(share / metro_share)
  ) %>%
  group_by(UU2020) %>%
  summarize(income_divergence_index = sum(divergence_component, na.rm = TRUE))

# Merge with housing divergence
merged_data <- metro_divergence %>%
  left_join(income_divergence, by = "UU2020")

# Plotting the relationship
ggplot(merged_data, aes(x = avg_divergence_value, y = income_divergence_index)) +
  geom_point(color = "#4b0082", size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    x = "Housing Divergence Index Value",
    y = "Income Divergence Index Value",
    title = "Housing Divergence vs. Income Segregation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

#Map of Divergence of Housing Tenure - Income Segregation Association
```{r}
# Load metro shapefile
metro_shapefile <- st_read("C:/Users/ohdaw/OneDrive/Documents/R_Projects/rental_desert/France/France_maps/uu_without_overseas/uu_without_overseas.shp")
## Assuming `income_divergence` and `metro_divergence` are calculated as per your method

# Determine thresholds for high/low segregation
housing_threshold <- median(metro_divergence$avg_divergence_value, na.rm = TRUE)
income_threshold <- median(income_divergence$income_divergence_index, na.rm = TRUE)

# Create a dataframe for segregation mapping
segregation_data <- metro_divergence %>%
  left_join(income_divergence, by = "UU2020") %>%
  mutate(
    segregation_type = case_when(
      avg_divergence_value >= housing_threshold & income_divergence_index >= income_threshold ~ "High Housing, High Income Segregation",
      avg_divergence_value >= housing_threshold & income_divergence_index < income_threshold ~ "High Housing, Low Income Segregation",
      avg_divergence_value < housing_threshold & income_divergence_index >= income_threshold ~ "Low Housing, High Income Segregation",
      TRUE ~ "Low Housing, Low Income Segregation"
    )
  )

# Ensure `segregation_data` is compatible for join
segregation_data_df <- as.data.frame(segregation_data)

# Join with the shapefile
map_data <- metro_shapefile %>%
  left_join(segregation_data_df, by = c("uu2020" = "UU2020"))

# Plot the map
ggplot(map_data) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = segregation_type), color = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "High Housing, High Income Segregation" = "#6a51a3",
    "High Housing, Low Income Segregation" = "#9ecae1",
    "Low Housing, High Income Segregation" = "#807dba",
    "Low Housing, Low Income Segregation" = "#bcbddc"
  )) +
  labs(title = "Metro Areas with High Housing and High Income Segregation",
       fill = "Segregation Type") +
  theme_minimal()
```

#Divergence of Housing Tenure Is Associated with Building Age Segregation
```{r}

# Convert necessary columns to numeric
iris_with_population_and_rental <- iris_with_population_and_rental %>%
  mutate(
    P21_RP_ACH19 = as.numeric(as.character(P21_RP_ACH19)),
    P21_RP_ACH45 = as.numeric(as.character(P21_RP_ACH45)),
    P21_RP_ACH70 = as.numeric(as.character(P21_RP_ACH70)),
    P21_RP_ACH90 = as.numeric(as.character(P21_RP_ACH90)),
    P21_RP_ACH05 = as.numeric(as.character(P21_RP_ACH05)),
    P21_RP_ACH18 = as.numeric(as.character(P21_RP_ACH18)),
    P21_RP_ACHTOT = as.numeric(as.character(P21_RP_ACHTOT))
  )

# Calculate the entropy index for building age
iris_with_population_and_rental <- iris_with_population_and_rental %>%
  mutate(
    share_ACH19 = P21_RP_ACH19 / P21_RP_ACHTOT,
    share_ACH45 = P21_RP_ACH45 / P21_RP_ACHTOT,
    share_ACH70 = P21_RP_ACH70 / P21_RP_ACHTOT,
    share_ACH90 = P21_RP_ACH90 / P21_RP_ACHTOT,
    share_ACH05 = P21_RP_ACH05 / P21_RP_ACHTOT,
    share_ACH18 = P21_RP_ACH18 / P21_RP_ACHTOT
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    building_age_entropy_index = -(
      sum(
        c(share_ACH19, share_ACH45, share_ACH70, share_ACH90, share_ACH05, share_ACH18) * 
        log(c(share_ACH19, share_ACH45, share_ACH70, share_ACH90, share_ACH05, share_ACH18)), 
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Summarize the entropy index at the metro level
building_age_divergence <- iris_with_population_and_rental %>%
  group_by(UU2020) %>%
  summarize(building_age_divergence_index = mean(building_age_entropy_index, na.rm = TRUE))


# Ensure building_age_divergence is a data frame
building_age_divergence_df <- as.data.frame(building_age_divergence)

# Merge with housing divergence
merged_data <- metro_divergence %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%  # Ensure metro_divergence is also a data frame
  left_join(building_age_divergence_df, by = "UU2020")

# Plotting the relationship
ggplot(merged_data, aes(x = avg_divergence_value, y = building_age_divergence_index)) +
  geom_point(color = "#4b0082", size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    x = "Housing Divergence Index Value",
    y = "Building Age Entropy Index Value",
    title = "Housing Divergence vs. Building Age Segregation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
